evidence: Both added claims are bounded by the platform layer, not by this handler, and neither is material on this endpoint. Latency: stamphog is a product DB (products/db_routing.yaml:2-3), so both its aliases run on the fail-open engine with connect_timeout=3 (posthog/settings/data_stores.py:212-220) and the breaker is on by default outside tests with threshold 3 failures per 30s window, 30s cooldown, single 5s probe lease (data_stores.py:176-190). Breaker state is shared through Redis across all pods (posthog/db_circuit_breaker.py:147-149, 171-213), so an outage costs at most three requests fleet-wide up to 3s each, then every call raises CircuitOpenError in microseconds (posthog/db_backends/failopen/base.py:28-35) and one half-open probe per 30s may burn another 3s (db_circuit_breaker.py:36-41, 74-78). That is the designed behaviour of every product-DB read in the repo; no caller anywhere special-cases CircuitOpenError (grep: only its definition at failopen/base.py:9), so the 'treat unavailability as an expected state' ask is a new convention, not a missed existing one. Log flood: the handler emits one logger.exception per settings serialization while the breaker is open (products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:77-81), but the endpoint has no poller: the frontend loads settings once on Code review scene mount (products/review_hog/frontend/reviewHogSettingsLogic.ts:954-956 -> loadAll 802) plus one PATCH per toggle and a reload only on PATCH failure (809-811); the 10s interval polls recent reviews, not settings (758-760). No other frontend caller exists (grep reviewHogSettingsRetrieve/PartialUpdate: only 446/448) and there is no review_hog MCP tools.yaml, and the scene's menu entry is flag-gated (products/review_hog/manifest.tsx:31). Volume is therefore bounded by human page loads on an alpha scene. Without the catch the same request would 500 with the same traceback, so the catch does not add error traffic; it only turns a 500 into a 200 with stamphog_connected=false, which the UI renders as a disabled toggle (products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1066). logger.exception on a swallowed failure is the house pattern in this product (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:141, 234, 273); the only intra-request inconsistency is that the sibling tolerant call in the same GET uses warning+exc_info (products/review_hog/backend/reviewer/lazy_seed.py:564-567), a style nit, not a production problem. The 'cache the flag' half restates cluster 7 (0/2 real).
notes: I would change my mind if the settings endpoint gained a polling caller or an MCP tool (turning one ERROR line per page load into a per-interval flood), if the stamphog aliases were shown to bypass the fail-open engine or run with the breaker disabled in production, or if the stamphog DB were known to accept connections but hang on queries (which the connect-path breaker does not cover and would make the 3s bound wrong).
